JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec. 166 of the M.V. Act, through his natural guardian,
seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, on 31.10.2021 at about 9.45 am., the petitioner being minor alongwith his grandfather were crossing the Dodda Banaswadi SCCH-24 main road, infront of S.R.Enterprises, from the Southern side to the Northern side and when both of them reached the other side of the road, the driver of the scooter bearing Reg.No.KA 03HY7052 came at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner coming from western side all of a sudden dashed against the petitioner, as a result he was knocked down to the ground and thrown to a distance of about 15 feet,
consequentially he sustained severe head injury, crush injury to his nose and abrasions on the face,
forehead and right hand with bleeding all over the face.

Immediately, he was shifted to nearby Asha Nursing Home, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Specialist Hospital at Bengaluru, wherein admitted as an inpatient and a MLC case was registered and discharged on the same day with an advise to come for C.T. scan and ENT consultation by keeping him under observation for 48 hours.
Accordingly, he was taken ENT consultant on 01.11.2021 for checkup and advise to go for plastic surgery later on, as the facial disfigurement has taken place on the nose and the face.
He was treated for more SCCH-24 than 3 months and now he has to be admitted for plastic surgery in order to correct the disfigurement of the face.
So far he had spend more than Rs.1,00,000/ towards treatment and hospital expenses and further sum of Rs.2,00,000/ is required for conducting plastic surgery.

3. It is further case of the Petitioner that, Prior to the accident he was a student and due to the accident injuries, he has developed fear conscious and is unable to concentrate in his studies and even today suffering huge pain and agony.
The K.R.Puram Police have registered a criminal case and filed charge sheet against the rider of the said scooter in Cr.No.136/2021 u/Sec. 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
Therefore, the 1st Respondent is the RC owner and the 2nd Respondent is the driver of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.

Master M.Mayur vs A.Chinnayyan on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47058489/
2 4.
In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents have appeared but not filed written statement and remained absent.

SCCH-24 5. Now the following points arise for determination:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the RTA alleged to have occurred on 31.10.2021 at about 9.45 a.m., opp to S.R.Enterprises, Doddabanaswadi main road,
Bengaluru560 043, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of scooter bearing Reg.No.KA 03 HY7052?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation as claimed? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom payable?
3.
What order
or award?

6. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, he has examined his natural guardian/grandfather Sri.M.Ramaswamy as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.15.
7.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

8. On hearing and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above points as follows:
SCCH-24 Point No.1: In the affirmative, Point No.2: Partly in the affirmative, Point No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 9. Point No.1:

It is the case of the Petitioner and the natural guardian/grandfather of the petitioner stated that, on 31.10.2021 at about 9.45 am., his minor grand son alongwith him were crossing the Dodda Banaswadi main road, infront of S.R.Enterprises, from the Southern side to the Northern side and when both of them reached the other side of the road, the driver of the scooter bearing Reg.No.KA03HY7052 came at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner coming from western side all of a sudden dashed against his grandson, as a result he was knocked down to the ground and thrown to a distance of about 15 feet, consequentially he sustained severe injuries and caused the accident.
The respondents have remained absent and not crossexamined the PW.1.

The natural guardian/grandfather of the minor Petitioner is SCCH-24 examined as PW.1 in support of the case and reiterated the petition averments in his examinationinchief and apart from oral evidence the petitioner has produced Exs.P.1 to P.5, P10 to P14 which are FIR, FIS, chargesheet,
spot sketch, spot mahazar, first information, further statement of first informant, PF No.29/2021,
ordersheet in CC No.267/2022 and MVA report.
The respondents have not chosen to cross examine the PW.1 and hence there is no contrary evidence to the case of the petitioner.
Further, the Exs.P.1 to P.5, P10 to P14 supports the case of the Petitioner.
The said documents being public documents have got presumptive value and after investigation the IO has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle.
The Ex.P.9/wound certificate shows that the Petitioner came to hospital with history of RTA and sustained simple and grievous injuries.

Therefore, there is no Master M.Mayur vs A.Chinnayyan on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47058489/
3 contrary evidence led by the Respondents.
Hence, the evidence of PW.1 and the documents produced as Exs.P.1 to P.5, P10 to P14 are considered in support of the case of the Petitioner.

From leading evidence the petitioner has proved SCCH-24 that due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle the accident occurred in which the petitioner has sustained simple and grievous injuries.
Accordingly point No.1 held in the affirmative.

10. Point No.2: The natural guardian/grandfather of the minor as PW.1 has further averred that,
on account of accident, his facial disfigurement which has taken place on the nose and face and they have caused him permanent disability and hence he is required for plastic surgery.
The Petitioner in this regard has entered into witness box and deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability.
Apart from that, he has also produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.9.

As per Ex.P.9, the Petitioner has sustained abrasion present over the outer aspect of lower third of right forearm, abrasion present over the outer aspect of middle third of right forearm,
abrasion present over the antero lateral asect of lower third of left leg, abrasion present over SCCH-24 the outer aspect of proximal part of left little finger, abrasion present over the front of left forehead, abrasion present over center of the glabella, abrasion present over the left side of upper lip, abrasion present just below the outer aspect of left eye brow, abrasion present over the outer aspect of left peri orbital region, laceration present over upper part of left forehead, which opinion that injury no.1 to 9 are simple and injury no.10 and 11 are grievous injuries in nature.
Ex.
P.8 / photos with CD shows that the disfigurement of face and nose of the petitioner.

Therefore,
the Petitioner is entitled compensation on the ground of disability by relying upon the dictum laid by the Hon'ble Apex court in Master Mallikarjun's case.

Age of the Petitioner:
11.
The Petitioner, in order to prove his age, has produced notarized copy of adhaar card as per Ex.P.15.
As per the said document, his date of birth mentioned as 08.07.2016.
The accident was occurred on 31.10.2021.

As SCCH-24 such, as on the date of accident the age of the Petitioner is considered as 5 years.
Quantum of Income and quantum of compensation 12.
The Petitioner, as on the date of accident, admittedly was a minor.
Therefore, he was not an earning anything.

As per the decision of Hon'ble supreme court reported in ILR 2014 Kar 4891 rendered in Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance having regard to relevant factors, precedents and approach of various Hon'ble high courts with regard to the compensation of the child victims, held that appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc., should be Rs.1,00,000/ disability up to 10%, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to whole body 3 lakhs: up to 60% 4 lakhs: up to 90% 5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be 6 lakhs.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case the Petitioner has not lead evidence of the doctor to prove the disability but as per Ex.P.9 the petitioner SCCH-24 sustained grievous injuries and hence he is suffering from disability and even if 0%10% is considered also the amount is fixed by the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ under the head of pain and suffering already undergone and to Master M.Mayur vs A.Chinnayyan on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47058489/
4 be undergone in future including loss of comforts amenities on account of disability.
The Petitioner was taken treatment in the hospital and also took follow up treatment as per the record.
This must have caused loss of some income and discomforts to the parents of the Petitioner during that period.
Therefore, his parents are entitled for a sum of Rs.15,000/ under the heads of loss of income and discomforts to the parents.
The guardian of the Petitioner has stated that they have spent considerable amount towards her conveyance and nourishment etc.,
Therefore, Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this head.

The Petitioner stated that they have spent Rs.1,00,000/
towards medical and other incidental expenses SCCH-24 and Rs.2,00,000/ is required for performing plastic surgery in future.
But, in this regard the Petitioner has produced 8 medical bills for Rs.4,824.55/ as per Ex.P.7 only for a sum of Rs.4,824.55/.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.4,824.55/ under the heads of medical expenses.

13. Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows: Sl. HEAD COMPENSATION No.
AMOUNT 1. Pain and suffering already Rs.1,00,000/ undergone and to be suffered in future including loss of comforts amenities on account of disability.
2. Discomforts, inconvenience and Rs.15,000/ Loss of earnings of the parent during the laid up period.

3. Medical Bills Rs.10,000/
4. Conveyance, attendant and Rs.4,824.55/ nourishment etc.
If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.1,30,000/ and same is the total compensation awarded under the different heads to the petitioner.

SCCH-24 LIABILITY:
14.

As discussed above the Respondents remained absent and as there is no insurance policy to the offending vehicle, hence the respondents being the owner and driver of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.8,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.1,30,000/ with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly Point No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.

POINT No.3:
15.
For the reasons and discussions made above and findings to the above points, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
SCCH-24

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,30,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Thirty Thousand only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the Master M.Mayur vs A.Chinnayyan on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47058489/
5 amount.
The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner and are directed to deposit the compensation amount within sixty days from the date of this award.

On deposit of compensation and interest, Rs.50,000/ shall be deposited in any N/S Bank in the name of petitioner till he attains majority and the remaining entire amount shall be released in favour of the guardian of the petitioner through epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment.
SCCH-24 Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
(Typed to my dictation directly on the computer by the Stenographer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 20th day of April 2023).
(Miss.B.T.ANNAPOORNESHWARI) C/c XXII Addl.,SCJ & ACMM BANGALORE.
